To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the LHC mono-jet searches are competitive with, and in certain cases superior to, the direct searches for dark matter masses up to 1 TeV, 2) the LHC limits on dark matter are comparable to the indirect limits from gamma-ray observations, and 3) the limits on dark matter from mono-jet searches can be significantly weaker than the limits from mono-photon searches if dark matter is coupled to the Higgs.

the mono-jet and mono-photon channels are competitive with direct detection experiments for spin-independent dark matter interactions with quarks, and that mono-photon searches are competitive for spin-dependent dark matter interactions with up-type quarks.

the ATLAS and CMS LHC searches are competitive with, and in some cases superior to, direct searches for dark matter, and are also competitive with indirect searches for dark matter in the mass range of 15-70GeV.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the possibility that the dark matter is a new weakly interacting particle that couples to Standard Model quarks and gluon, and is produced at the LHC via the annihilation of a Standard Model quark and antiquark.
the question whether dark matter can be detected in the LHC mono-jet channel, and if so, under what conditions.
the question of how much we can learn about dark matter by looking for missing energy signatures at the LHC, and we find that the answer is "quite a lot"
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

LHC searches for mono-jets and mono-photons provide competitive limits on spin-dependent dark matter-nucleon couplings and on dark matter-quark and -gluon couplings, and they provide the strongest bounds on dark matter-Standard model interactions for a wide range of models and for dark matter masses below 100 GeV.

the LHC has already provided strong constraints on dark matter models, and that the next generation of mono-jet searches will be able to probe a significant part of the parameter space of models with thermal dark matter.
LHC constraints on effective dark matter-quark/gluon couplings are competitive with, and in certain cases superior to, limits on direct and indirect searches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mono-jet searches provide a very competitive probe of dark matter models with large spin-independent scattering off nucleons, and the invisible Higgs decay searches provide a very powerful probe of models with large spin-dependent scattering off nucleons.
the LHC is an important complement to direct and indirect dark matter detection experiments, and that the LHC can probe dark matter masses up to the multi-TeV scale.
LHC searches for missing energy signatures are very sensitive to dark matter interactions with quarks and gluon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LHC has the potential to discover or constrain dark matter in the near future, and that the LHC will continue to play a leading role in dark matter searches in the coming years.
LHC mono-jet searches are sensitive to dark matter-quark interactions, and that they are competitive, or better, than existing direct and indirect dark matter searches.
the LHC is an excellent probe of dark matter, and that it can be used to set competitive limits on the dark matter-Standard model couplings, particularly for masses above 100-200 GeV.
